children: The Treasury Department's $22 billion 30-year auction today will test whether investors are ready to lock up their money while bond rates are at their highest levels since 2007, BMO analysts say in a research note. Bessent's line-in-the-sand for long-bond rates looks to be 5.3%, meaning today's reopening will be a potentially crucial litmus test for his department's new activist approach to debt management, the analysts say. They expect this to be the highest yielding 30-year auction since the financial crisis. Yesterday's 10-year reopening cleared at the highest yield since 2008, the analysts say. (dean.seal@wsj.com)
